concept.name: Maturity date
concept.definition: The specified date on which the principal (face value) of a debt instrument such as a bond is scheduled to be repaid to the investor; for futures, 'maturity' refers to the period within which the contract can be settled by delivery.
concept.intuition: The maturity date is the loan's end date: it is when the borrower's promise to hand back the principal comes due.
concept.mechanics: A bond pays coupons on a regular schedule until maturity, when the final coupon plus the face value are paid. Time to maturity shortens as time passes, and together with the coupon rate it drives interest-rate sensitivity: longer maturities generally carry greater interest rate risk.
concept.failure_modes: Selling before maturity exposes the holder to whatever price the market dictates, so 'getting your principal back' holds only if the bond is held to maturity and the issuer does not default; callable bonds can be retired before the stated maturity.
concept.misconceptions: Maturity date is not the same as duration: a coupon bond's duration is always shorter than its maturity (only a zero-coupon bond's duration equals its maturity), because some cash arrives earlier as coupons.
concept.example: A 10-year Treasury note issued in 2026 pays interest every six months and repays its face value on its 2036 maturity date; if sold in 2030, the investor receives the then-market price instead of par.
